items.title: Apple sues OpenAI, accuses ex-employees of stealing trade secrets
items.author: stock_toaster
items.summary: Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, accusing two former employees of stealing trade secrets. The lawsuit claims confidential information was taken to aid OpenAI's hardware development. The relationship between Apple and OpenAI deteriorated after a planned integration of AI technology fell through.

items.title: QuadRF can spot drones and see WiFi through my wall
items.author: speckx
items.summary: QuadRF is a phased-array radio that can detect drones and see WiFi signals through walls. It uses advanced signal processing and a Raspberry Pi 5. It was developed by Martin McCormick.

items.title: Meta pulls new AI image feature after days of backlash
items.author: cdrnsf
items.summary: Meta halted its AI image feature, Muse, following privacy and consent concerns, acknowledging it "missed the mark" on user consent. The feature, which used public Instagram photos, was disabled three days after launch. This decision highlights the importance of consent in AI-generated content.

items.title: Choosing the Right AI Agent Memory Strategy: A Decision-Tree Approach
items.author: eigenBasis
items.summary: To choose the right AI agent memory strategy, consider explicit, durable memory layers for continuity and context, alongside simple conversation history for immediate tasks. Effective memory strategies use both daily and long-term memory for optimal performance.

items.title: GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra produces proof of the Cycle Double Cover Conjecture [pdf]
items.author: scrlk
items.summary: The Cycle Double Cover Conjecture was proven in 2024. The proof was published in a research paper. The conjecture states that every bridgeless graph has a cycle cover using exactly two cycles per edge.

items.title: An update on residential proxies and the scraper situation
items.author: chmaynard
items.summary: Residential proxies are legal for scraping public sites if used ethically, with high success rates and reliability. ScraperAPI offers millions of residential proxies for web scraping. Legality depends on consent and respect for site terms.

items.title: SpaceX wants to launch 100k more Starlink satellites for 100x the bandwidth
items.author: CrankyBear
items.summary: SpaceX plans to launch 100,000 additional Starlink satellites to achieve 100 times the bandwidth. This expansion aims to provide global coverage and enhanced connectivity. The initiative is expected to significantly improve internet access worldwide.

items.title: AI 2040: Plan A
items.author: kschaul
items.summary: Plan A is a recommendation for avoiding AI-driven catastrophe, not a prediction. It involves international coordination and expert input. It aims for a flourishing future with AI.

items.title: After 7 years in production, Scarf has reluctantly moved away from Haskell
items.author: aviaviavi
items.summary: After 7 years in production, Scarf has moved away from Haskell for new product development, opting for Python to leverage the latest AI tools. They still respect Haskell and continue to use it in existing systems.

items.title: In Emacs, everything looks like a service
items.author: kickingvegas
items.summary: Emacs is designed for extensive customization and can be used for many tasks, often running as a daemon for efficient access. The `emacsclient` allows for faster interaction. Running Emacs as a systemd service enhances its lifecycle management.

items.title: Lost city discovered beneath Egypt's desert with ancient church
items.author: Bender
items.summary: A lost city with an ancient church was discovered beneath Egypt's desert, hidden for 1,600 years, with intact homes and coins. The find was made in 2026.

items.title: A love letter to flashcards
items.author: surprisetalk
items.summary: Flashcards are effective tools for spaced repetition learning. They help reinforce memory through regular review. Popular software like Anki enhances their use.

items.title: Snails' teeth beats spider silk as nature's strongest material (2015)
items.author: simonebrunozzi
items.summary: Limpet teeth, composed of iron-filled goethite nanofibers in a chitin matrix, are the strongest known biological material, surpassing spider silk and Kevlar. This strength allows them to scrape food from rocks. Despite not matching man-made materials like graphene, they are far superior to Kevlar and carbon fibers.

items.title: GhostLock, a stack-UAF that has existed in ALL Linux distributions for 15 years
items.author: djfergus
items.summary: GhostLock (CVE-2026-43499) is a long-standing Linux kernel vulnerability present in all distributions since 2011. It allows an attacker to write to arbitrary memory addresses. The issue was fixed in April 2026.

items.title: How the terrorist group Boko Haram uses frontier AI
items.author: imustachyou
items.summary: Boko Haram uses frontier AI, including models like ChatGPT, to plan attacks and design explosive devices, based on interviews with former members. This misuse of AI highlights a real and emerging threat. For more details, refer to the full report from the Cambridge Programme on AI Science & Policy.

Then we went our separate ways, got married, had kids, focused on other things.

items.summary: In 2026, a project revives a 2001 college band using AI to reimagine their music. The lead singer collaborates with AI to recreate their original songs. The project explores AI's role in the arts.

items.title: Show HN: Frugon – Find which LLM calls a cheaper model could handle (local, MIT)

items.text:

I realised I had to do something about it else I'd have to double my spend. So I decided to start tracking my cost per task type. This revealed that a lot of my spend went to searches/scans or simple things like scouting tasks.

items.summary: Frugon is a CLI tool to analyze and compare costs of LLM calls, suggesting cheaper alternatives. It uses local MIT research for savings estimates. Available on GitHub.

items.title: Show HN: Reverse-engineering web apps into agent tools
items.author: pancomplex
items.text:
Hey HN! We built a browser-based agent that runs inside an authenticated web app, watches how the app calls its own APIs, and automatically turns those into agent tools. You can think of it as an auto-generated MCP server that self-updates as the host app changes.

The result is a skilled AI assistant that actually integrates deeply with any product (not just chat and RAG) with minimal effort.

Check out these short demos below that show the agent in software you're probably familiar with
items.summary: A browser-based agent reverse-engineers authenticated web apps, automatically converting their APIs into agent tools, updating as the app changes. This tool can generate faster, more efficient scraper scripts and is showcased on Hacker News and Reddit. The concept was also presented at NIDC 2025.

items.title: Punk, or why I don't stream anymore
items.author: surprisetalk
items.summary: George Hotz stopped streaming because he believes spectacle and performativity have destroyed authentic hacker culture. He argues that AI contributes to this by offering false engagement.

items.title: Prismata: Confining cross-site prompt injection in web agents
items.author: zhinit
items.summary: Prismata is a defense mechanism for web agents that confines cross-site prompt injection by enforcing contextual least privilege and structural confinement. It limits what the agent can see and do, preventing malicious content from hijacking the agent. This approach helps secure web agents against prompt injection attacks.

items.title: Materials innovation has a scale-up problem, not discovery
items.author: groznyj
items.summary: Materials innovation struggles with scaling up, not discovery. Efficient regulations and standards are needed. Advanced informatics aids in scaling.

items.title: Postgres locks do not scale
items.author: timetoogo
items.summary: Postgres locks can hinder scalability due to blocking operations, especially with many concurrent transactions. Lock contention increases with more users, slowing performance. Scaling often requires optimizing transactions to reduce lock duration.

items.title: Show HN: SubjectiveZero, an open-source agentic node editor for creative coding
items.author: tasoeur
items.text:
Hey there,

I've been building creation tools for a while and some common design challenge is to figure out the right level of abstraction for your tool. You can always make it super advanced and complex with low level concepts (shader composition, actual code etc.) but then you get something with a high complex
items.summary: SubjectiveZero is an open-source node editor for creative coding. It aims to provide the right level of abstraction for tool creation. It was showcased on Hacker News.

items.title: Frog bacterium wiped out cancer tumors in mice with a single dose
items.author: dcyfr
items.summary: A bacterium from frog guts, Ewingella americana, wiped out cancer tumors in mice with one dose. It directly kills cancer cells and boosts immune response. Human trials are next.

items.title: Please don't discontinue Gemini 2.5 Flash
items.author: NickDob
items.summary: Gemini 2.5 Flash is valued for its performance and cost-effectiveness. Users are concerned about its discontinuation. Gemini 2.5 Flash is preferred over newer versions for specific tasks.
